chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Safwan, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade Al-Muhalakah and Al-Muzabana. I asked: 'What are they?' He said: 'That the crop of the palm trees is purchased with dates, and the crop is purchased with wheat.'

key_terms.الْمُحَاقَلَة: Sale of unharvested grain crop for measured dry grain
key_terms.الْمُزَابَنَة: Sale of unharvested fruit crop for measured dried fruit
key_terms.حَمْلُ النَّخْلِ: The crop/bearing of the palm trees

ai.seo_question: What are Al-Muhalakah and Al-Muzabana in Islamic trade law?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Prophet’s prohibition of *Al-Muhalakah* (selling unripe fruit for ripe fruit) and *Al-Muzabana* (selling unharvested grain for a different grain), highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on avoiding *gharar* (uncertainty) in agricultural contracts. The hadith serves as a foundational text for jurists distinguishing between spot transactions and forward sales of crops, ensuring fairness in pre-harvest exchanges. It underscores the practical application of commercial justice in early Islamic society, where crop yields were unpredictable.
